newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey drafts step to clean up rights record.
newsitem.headline: Turkey drafts step to clean up rights record.

text.p: Turkey's Islamist-led government has submitted to parliament a draft law shortening the initial period of police detention for suspected criminals, the Justice Ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.

Under the draft law, the maximum period someone can be detained by police without formal charges being filed will be cut to seven days from the current 30 days in the mainly Kurdish provinces under emergency rule.
Human rights activists say that the initial period of detention is when suspects are most at risk from torture -- something activists say is systematic in Turkey. The Turkish government denies this.
In the rest of the country, the detention period will be shortened to four days from the current two weeks.
But under the draft, police can get a three-day extension of the detention period.

"As is known the period of detention by police forces of suspected criminals, is a subject on which the Council of Europe and the European Parliament feel great sensitivity. This draft law was prepared...in order to comply with the rules of the states who make up the Council of Europe," the statement said.
The European Parliament in October voted in the first reading of the 1997 European Union budget to block hundreds of millions of dollars of aid to Turkey, partly because of its human rights record.
The government has not given any indication when this draft law will be submitted to parliament.
